_comment: How each ASD-STE100 Issue 9 rule is treated by ste-lint.py. This file is our
classification, not part of the standard. Rule text itself is never stored here.
tier:     enforced  the linter decides, and a violation fails the run
flagged   the linter warns, and the agent resolves it or says why not
judgment  no machine can decide it, so the agent attests to it
modes:    which modes fail on this rule. ste-general keeps the structural subset
plus the denylist. ste-strict adds the dictionary allowlist.
check:    the ste-lint.py check id that implements the rule, or null when the
rule is only carried here for the reference files and the checklist.

1.1.short: Use approved words, technical nouns, or technical verbs

1.2.short: Use an approved word only as its specified part of speech

1.3.short: Use an approved word only with its approved meaning

1.4.short: Use only approved forms of verbs and adjectives

1.6.short: An unapproved word must be a technical noun

1.7.short: Do not use a technical noun as a verb

1.8.short: Technical nouns come from your company or field

1.9.short: Select a short technical noun that is easy to understand

1.10.short: No regional, slang, or jargon technical nouns

1.13.short: Do not use a technical verb as a noun

2.1.short: Multi-word nouns of no more than three words

2.2.short: Write a technical noun of more than three words in full

3.1.short: Use only the verb forms given in the dictionary

3.2.short: Use only the permitted verb forms and tenses

3.3.short: Use the past participle as an adjective

3.4.short: No complex verb constructions from stacked auxiliaries

3.5.short: The “-ing” form only as a technical noun or modifier

3.7.short: Use a verb for an action, not a noun

4.2.short: Do not omit words or use contractions

4.3.short: Use a vertical list for complex text

4.4.short: Use connecting words between related sentences

4.5.short: Use an article or demonstrative adjective before a noun

5.3.short: Write instructions in the imperative form

5.4.short: Put a condition before its command

6.2.short: Use key words and phrases for logical structure

6.4.short: Use paragraphs to show related information

6.6.short: No paragraph of more than six sentences

7.2.short: Start a safety instruction with the command or condition

7.3.short: Explain the risk or possible result

8.4.short: In a vertical list a colon ends a sentence

8.5.short: Parenthetical text counts as one word

8.6.short: Numbers, units, abbreviations, and quoted text count as one word

8.7.short: A hyphenated word counts as one word

9.1.short: Rewrite the sentence when word-for-word replacement fails

H.2.short: House rule: replace a word the dictionary does not approve
